items.q: Can sound travel through a vacuum?
items.correct: No — sound needs particles (a medium) to travel.
items.misconception: Yes, sound travels through empty space.
items.random_wrong: Sound travels faster in a vacuum than in air.
items.why: Unlike light, sound cannot cross a vacuum because it needs a material to vibrate.

items.q: In a transverse wave, how do the particles move?
items.correct: At right angles to the direction the wave travels.
items.misconception: In the same direction the wave travels.
items.why: Transverse: vibrations perpendicular to travel (e.g. light). Longitudinal: parallel (e.g. sound).

items.q: Which travels faster, light or sound?
items.correct: Light, by a huge margin (~3×10⁸ vs ~340 m/s).
items.random_wrong: They travel at the same speed.
items.why: You see lightning before hearing thunder because light is far faster than sound.
